title: Flatness localizes at prime localizations
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and let $M$ be an $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. For every prime $\mathfrak q\subset A$ write $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap R$ and use the localizations [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. If $M$ is flat over $R$, then $M_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $R_{\mathfrak p}$ for every prime $\mathfrak q$ of $A$, where the localizations use the induced module structure.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 10.39.18, Tag 00HT, part (6), only-if direction

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $A$ and put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap R$. Apply the localization-preserves-flatness statement to the multiplicative subset $A\setminus\mathfrak q$. It gives that $M_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $R$. The induced $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module structure on $M_{\mathfrak q}$ exists because every element of $R\setminus\mathfrak p$ maps outside $\mathfrak q$ and is therefore invertible in $A_{\mathfrak q}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 10.39.18, Tag 00HT, part (6), only-if direction

proof.text: The canonical map $R\to R_{\mathfrak p}$ is the localization at $R\setminus\mathfrak p$, and $M_{\mathfrak q}$ is an $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module. By the equivalence of flatness over a ring and over its localization for modules over the localized ring, $M_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $R_{\mathfrak p}$.
